ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based pre-incorporation screening under Law 10/2010, SEPBLAC guidance and EU AML Directives: all directors, shareholders, UBOs, co-venturers and material commercial counterparties must be screened against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, US OFAC SDN list, domestic Spanish watch-lists and PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds justification, applies to PEPs, high-risk non-resident jurisdictions, maritime installment letter-of-credit structures and escrow payment arrangements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) via CIRCE and the official electronic registry platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate denomination must be expressed in Spanish using the Spanish alphabet; foreign-language names must be transliterated into Spanish phonetic spelling, unified as a single denomination, and the legal-form suffix must be 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' The name must be distinctive and not misleading as to legal form, activity, or public status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A negative name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central is valid for 90 days and cannot be extended; after expiry a new application must be filed. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may immediately file a revised request with two or more alternative names. Where rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant may apply for prior ministerial authorization from the competent administrative authority. Any adverse administrative ruling on the name application may be appealed by recurso de alzada to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado within one month under Ley 39/2015 de Procedimiento Administrativo Común.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole corporate registered office for an ISIC 3011 shipbuilding entity. A physical operational shipyard, maritime industrial land, port authority approvals, and effective management presence in Spain are required for statutory licensing, tax substance, and commercial credibility. A virtual office may only serve as an ancillary administrative correspondence address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: quantified at 80-90% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months of operation, particularly by Port Authority of Spain, maritime safety authorities, the labor inspectorate, environmental enforcement units, and municipal licensing officers.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and paid-up capital of 3,000 euros; no escrow account mandated for private SL entities
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors resolves: (1) To accept the full subscription of the share capital amounting to 3,000 euros by the incorporators; (2) To establish the registered office at the address detailed in the articles of association; (3) To appoint [full name] as Managing Director and [full name] as Director; (4) To empower the Managing Director to execute all incorporation documents, apply for tax identification (CIF), and pursue all necessary industrial and environmental licenses; (5) To schedule the first General Shareholders' Meeting within the statutory period. Adopted unanimously on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage notary to draft public deed of incorporation including full articles of association, share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. Execute deed and subscribe shares therein.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise formal defects and resubmit to notary

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Departamento de Gestión Tributaria and Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales. Principal portal: AEAT Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. The Spanish tax identification number is the Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF); the Spanish VAT identification number is generally the NIF prefixed by ES for intra-Community transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional NIF before or during incorporation and a definitive NIF after registration with the Mercantile Registry. The application is normally filed electronically with AEAT using Modelo 036, supported by the deed of incorporation, articles of association, registered office details, identification of directors and beneficial owners, and evidence of registry filing or registration. A foreign corporate shareholder must obtain a Spanish NIF for tax dealings by filing Modelo 036 through its Spanish representative, authorized attorney or qualified electronic representative. Foreign corporate documents generally require apostille or legalization and a sworn Spanish translation unless an applicable treaty or EU simplification applies. Registration for the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and inclusion in the VIES system is requested through Modelo 036 and is required for qualifying intra-Community supplies and acquisitions. An EORI number is separately required for customs operations and is obtained from AEAT customs authorities. VAT registration must be completed before commencing taxable activities when the entity acts as a Spanish taxable person; non-established businesses register where Spanish VAT obligations arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no general United States-style check-the-box election. An SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer. Available statutory regimes and elections may include the consolidated tax regime for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers, demergers and other reorganizations, the Spanish holding-company participation exemption subject to statutory conditions, the Canary Islands special regimes where geographically applicable, and other expressly regulated sectoral regimes. Tax transparency applies only to specified legal forms and circumstances and does not generally convert an SL into a pass-through entity. The Spanish tonnage tax regime is principally designed for qualifying shipping activities and is not automatically available to a shipbuilding manufacturer. Hybrid mismatch restrictions under the Corporate Income Tax Law may deny deductions or impose inclusion where the statutory anti-hybrid conditions are met; there is no elective hybrid-mismatch classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT under the Union Customs Code. Spain applies EU VAT rules through the Spanish VAT Law, Law 37/1992, and related regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold applies for Spanish VAT registration. The effective registration threshold is EUR 0 for a person commencing or carrying out an independent economic activity that creates Spanish VAT obligations. Spain generally requires registration before the relevant taxable activity or transaction, subject to specific place-of-supply and non-established-business rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all VAT invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted subject to authenticity, integrity, legibility, recipient acceptance where required, and retention controls. The Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información or SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including businesses with turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups and certain entities using the monthly refund regime, to transmit invoice-book data electronically to AEAT, generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory exceptions. The electronic invoicing framework for private-sector business-to-business transactions introduced by Law 18/2022 requires implementing regulations and phased compliance. Spain also has regulated electronic invoicing software and invoice-record integrity requirements under Law 11/2021 and Royal Decree 1007/2023, including the VERI*FACTU framework and anti-tampering controls; these requirements are not equivalent to universal advance invoice clearance. Export customs declarations and exit confirmations are processed electronically through AEAT customs systems and EU customs infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spain to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct under Article 21 of Law 37/1992, provided the statutory exporter, transport, customs and documentary conditions are satisfied. The supplier must retain evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory, normally through the electronic export declaration and customs exit results, together with commercial and transport records linking the goods to the invoice. Intra-Community supplies are generally exempt with the right to deduct under separate conditions, including valid customer VAT identification and transport evidence. Services supplied to a non-EU business may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under place-of-supply rules rather than technically zero-rated; the analysis depends on customer status, service type, location, and use-and-enjoyment rules. Shipbuilding contracts require transaction-specific analysis because goods, installation, work on vessels, engineering, leasing and ancillary services may have different VAT treatment. Input VAT refunds are claimed through periodic VAT returns, with accelerated monthly refunds available to eligible taxpayers registered in REDEME and other statutory refund procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration accepted by Spanish or other EU customs authorities, including the Movement Reference Number and customs export records
Electronic customs exit confirmation or equivalent proof that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, VAT treatment and relevant export references
Transport evidence appropriate to the shipment, such as bill of lading, sea waybill, CMR, air waybill or carrier confirmation
Packing list, delivery records and serial or hull identification records where relevant to a shipyard delivery
Contract, purchase order and shipping instructions demonstrating the link between the taxable supply and the export
EORI numbers and customs representation records where applicable
Proof of payment or commercial settlement records where relevant to audit substantiation; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory Spanish VAT export document
For qualifying services, evidence of customer establishment, contractual scope, place of supply, recipient VAT or tax status, and offshore performance or use where relevant
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain does not generally impose a 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement as a condition for export VAT exemption. AEAT may deny or claw back the exemption where customs exit, transport, customer, contractual or accounting evidence is incomplete, inconsistent or fabricated. The resulting assessment may include unpaid VAT, late-payment interest and penalties under the General Tax Law, including penalties for failure to pay or for incorrect tax returns that commonly range from 50% to 100% of the improperly unpaid tax and may reach 150% in aggravated cases, subject to statutory classification and mitigation rules. Failure to issue or retain compliant invoices may generate additional penalties. Fraudulent customs declarations may trigger customs debt, import or export-related sanctions, confiscation or other measures under the Union Customs Code and Spanish customs law. Criminal exposure may arise for aggravated tax fraud or customs offenses where statutory monetary thresholds and intent requirements are met. A genuine export that is later recharacterized as a domestic Spanish supply is assessed at the applicable VAT rate, ordinarily 21%, plus interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España – the national central bank of Spain, exercising supervisory powers over credit institutions and enforcing balance-of-payments and foreign-investment statistical reporting as an agent of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation; acts within the Single Supervisory Mechanism and the European System of Central Banks under the ECB framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Spain for both current and capital account transactions. Spain applies the EU capital-movements liberalization principle, and no prior foreign-exchange authorization is required for ordinary trade settlements, profit repatriation, or dividend distributions to non-residents. However, the Tax Administration requires non-resident withholding at source (generally 19% for dividends under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime, subject to applicable tax treaty relief), and the Bank of Spain mandates statistical declaration for capital transactions and large-value settlements through authorized resident banks. Profit-remittance hurdles are limited to documentary proof of compliance with corporate income tax and AML-source-of-funds requirements; no remittance licensing or queue exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or fixed conversion ratio of export proceeds. A resident shipyard may freely hold and dispose of foreign currency. Nevertheless, the exporter must correctly classify every collection in the Balance of Payments statistical declaration (DEO – Declaración Estadística de Operaciones) filed with the Bank of Spain through its settlement bank; export receipts exceeding EUR 50,000 or equivalent require itemised declaration, and the invoice, transport document, and customs export entry (DUA) must be retained for audit. For letter-of-credit instalments, the shipyard must ensure the receiving bank has the correct purpose code for goods exported out of Spain and reconcile the settlement with the export declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in EUR plus segregated USD settlement sub-account; Escrow/Collection Account for maritime instalments
Operational Treasury Account; Capital Escrow Account for shareholders' equity injection
Operational Account with electronic-banking trade module; Escrow for LC-backed progress payments
Operational Account and export collection account with advanced FX conversion line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury anchor. A Spanish resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada in the commercial shipbuilding industry cannot rely on a non-EU or exclusively offshore fintech EMI for statutory clearing functions, because such providers are not Banco de España-regulated entities, cannot offer an IBAN issued under Spanish credit-institution rules, and are not capacitated to issue or settle commercial letters of credit. EU-licensed EMIs with passporting rights under PSD2 may be onboarded as a secondary payment channel for limited operational disbursements, but the core cross-border treasury, escrow, and LC operations must be routed through a Tier-1 credit institution established in Spain or an authorized EU branch with concomitant Bank of Spain filing capabilities. Furthermore, enhanced due diligence in the shipbuilding sector requires a regulated bank with at least a physical compliance office and reporting gateway to the Bank of Spain.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and in-person KYC interview are, in practice, mandatory for a legal entity with multiple non-resident shareholders, large instalment-based export contracts, and medium-risk / enhanced-due-diligence classification. The appointed directors (administradores) and at least one principal UBO must appear with valid NIE, passport, and proof of residential address for a face-to-face compliance interview in a Spanish bank branch. Remote-video onboarding may be allowed under Spanish AML law for low-risk clients only; for an industrial exporter involved in commercial shipbuilding, Tier-1 banks uniformly apply the physical-interview rule. Non-resident directors can appoint a local attorney-in-fact with an apostilled and translated notarial power, provided that the Spanish attorney appears physically and the UBO certification is authenticated; the compliance department will additionally require evidence of the directors' identity and authority from the Companies Register (Registro Mercantil).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial shipbuilder with large USD-denominated instalment payments routed through a series of non-resident ship-owning SPVs in high-risk or tax-haven jurisdictions (e.g., Panama, Marshall Islands, UAE).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The bank must receive a complete corporate tree and UBO declaration under Spanish Law 10/2010; audited financial statements of the Spanish SL; the shipbuilding contract with OECD-compliant commercial terms; certificates of good standing, constitutional documents and register extracts of each SPV counterparty; commercial invoices; customs export declarations (DUA); letters of intent or charter-party agreements demonstrating the underlying vessel's beneficial end-user; and an independent AML/risk memorandum prepared by a Spanish compliance adviser explaining the legitimate commercial purpose of the offshore routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value unsecured commercial letters of credit or escrow instalments exceeding the company's reported revenue and balance-sheet equity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank must obtain an independent auditor's confirmation of the vessel construction costs, progress milestones and payment schedule; bank-verified statement of the SL's own capital structure; evidence of shareholder loans or equity injection with complete source-of-funds trail (original bank statements, notarised loan agreements, tax declarations of the shareholders, and capital-movement declaration to the Bank of Spain); and a third-party valuation certificate of the vessel under construction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent payments to sub-contractors and equipment suppliers with cross-border names and invoicing similar to trade-based money laundering indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full procurement matrix linking each subcontractor to the specific vessel project; signed sub-contract agreements; customs import declarations for equipment and materials; evidence of goods receipts and verifiable delivery confirmation; and statutory VAT declaration (AEAT) plus annual accounts showing that the transactions flow through the company's production cost structure. Directors must be prepared to explain any late payment or early repayment deviation with supporting board minutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure and foreign directors signing without physical presence in Spain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a notarised and apostilled board resolution naming the authorized signatories; NIE and passport of each signatory; original parent company incorporation documents and UBO register extraction; a tax-residence certificate of the foreign shareholder issued by its domestic tax authority; a PKI digital certificate for the Spanish representative; and a commitment to comply with Bank of Spain statistical reporting and Spanish corporate governance transparency duties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing for a capital contribution from a non-resident shareholder is a SWIFT MT103 euro or USD transfer to the SL's Spanish operational account, referencing the purpose code for capital or equity injection as defined by the Bank of Spain (e.g., statistical concept 'Inversión en participaciones y otros valores' – J-1 capital-movement declaration). The transfer must originate from the shareholder's own bank account in its jurisdiction; all supporting documentation (shareholder resolution, notarised capital increase deed, UBO certificate, bank statements evidencing the source of funds, and proof of registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs if the foreign investment exceeds notification thresholds) must be filed and retained. For amounts above EUR 100,000, a completed Declaración Previa de Movimiento de Capitales with the Banco de España is required; the bank will require the goods/vessel construction project number and the final destination of funds before clearing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and disbursements to equipment vendors, the primary rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 bank payment orders for ordinary procurement obligations, with ISO 20022 or purpose code indicating 'trade in goods' and the customs document reference; (b) SWIFT MT700/MT710 commercial letters of credit opened through the Spanish bank's correspondent network in favour of equipment manufacturers, with reimbursements settled via MT103; (c) inward and outward documentary collections (MT400/MT2??) to support maritime milestone invoicing; and (d) escrow releases driven by mutually authenticated commercial acceptance certificates under the shipbuilding contract. Every disbursement must be matched against the VAT/general customs declaration and the Bank of Spain declaration where applicable. The SL must maintain a ‘settlement ledger’ per vessel to allow the bank to distinguish the underlying business purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts for immediate USD/EUR conversion
FX outright forwards (deferred delivery, maturity-matched to vessel instalments)
FX swaps (swap of principal and interest streams between USD and EUR for construction funding)
European-style currency options (plain vanilla USD/EUR calls and puts) to hedge firm or anticipated procurement exposure
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term installon-based financing covered by an underlying export credit or facility agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office (Registro Mercantil Provincial), coordinated with the Central Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the shareholders' meeting within six months of fiscal year-end and deposited within one month of approval. For a calendar-year SL: approval by 30 June and deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a fine under Article 283 of the Spanish Companies Act of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; continued non-deposit causes the Registry to open a preventive closure note (cierre provisional), blocks subsequent registry filings, and may ultimately support judicial dissolution proceedings. Spain does not operate an automatic administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months and 25 days after the tax year-end. For a calendar-year SL: 1 July to 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior notice incurs a surcharge under Article 27 of the General Tax Law of 5% to 20% plus late-payment interest; delayed filing after formal notice attracts 1% per month up to 15%; non-payment of the resulting tax debt can support penalties of 50% to 150% of the tax due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 January following the calendar year for VAT taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers the same General Tax Law late-filing surcharge regime (5% to 20% plus interest); AEAT may also issue an official VAT assessment and impose proportional penalties of 50% to 100% of the under-assessed amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third-party transactions information return (Modelo 347), if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 February to 20 March following the calendar year; the deadline is extended to the next business day if 20 March falls on a non-working day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or inaccurate records attract a EUR 300 penalty per item, with a minimum of EUR 1,500 and a maximum of EUR 20,000; persistent non-filing exposes the company to formal reassessment and collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding summary return (Modelo 190), if payroll or director fees were paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 31 January following the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs surcharges and interest under the General Tax Law; failure to report withheld amounts may result in AEAT collection of the withheld tax together with penalties for material omission under Articles 191 and 198.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate beneficial ownership confirmation attached to annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry / Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidad Real) within the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual accounts deposit; for a calendar-year SL, by 31 July. Any share transfer that changes UBO must be reflected in the Register of Members and updated in the annual confirmation no later than the next filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or omitted UBO data may be treated as an AML infringement under Law 10/2010, attracting substantial administrative fines; the Commercial Registry may also refuse the annual accounts filing or record a preventive note until the UBO statement is corrected.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL must appoint an independent auditor if, for at least two consecutive fiscal years, it meets at least two of the following at year-end: total assets above EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, financial entities, entities with securities listed in Spanish or EU markets, and entities otherwise required by law or shareholders' resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable) under the Commercial Code and the Spanish Companies Act. Small entities may use the SME PGC, and micro-entities may use the PGC Micro for lower-volume reporting. Consolidated accounts, if applicable, must follow IFRS as endorsed by the EU when required by law, otherwise the consolidation rules of Spanish GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not impose a standalone annual UBO tax return. The beneficial-ownership declaration is embedded in the annual accounts deposit: the SL must identify every individual who directly or indirectly owns more than 25% of the share capital or controls the company, and must confirm that information as of year-end. Share transfers altering UBO must be recorded in the Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios), formalized if required by the SL transfer rules, and reflected in the next annual confirmation. Failure to update UBO data is a continuing AML compliance breach.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores / Register of directorships)
Register of Contracts with Directors (Libro Registro de Contratos con Administradores)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventario y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 330 - USD 875 per annum (EUR 300 - EUR 800); higher band of USD 875 - USD 1,640 (EUR 800 - EUR 1,500) in Madrid and Barcelona for registered office and compliance-agent services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,360 - USD 13,080 per audit cycle (EUR 4,000 - EUR 12,000) for a shipyard SL requiring a statutory audit; lower-end audits apply to smaller companies that voluntarily appoint an auditor.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (general Corporate Income Tax rate under Article 29.1 Ley 27/2014)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created entities in the first two tax periods with positive taxable base, provided that the entity creates jobs and undertakes material commercial activity; investment tax credit of 15% for qualifying shipbuilding assets and capital equipment used in vessel construction; R&D and technological innovation credit up to 25-42%; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; special tax lease regime for shipbuilders.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiration (indefinite carryforward). Offsetting is subject to quantitative limits: 70% of the taxable base for entities with net turnover under €10 million; 60% for turnover between €10 million and €20 million; 50% for turnover of €20 million or more; a minimum of €1 million may always be offset.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Modelo 200) – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return; submitted electronically through the AEAT electronic filing portal (Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the fiscal year. For calendar-year taxpayers, the deadline is 25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover: aggregate billed revenue from shipbuilding, repair, and related maritime engineering services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a permanent establishment (PE) in Spain, report Spanish-source turnover attributable to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary activity income: operating revenue recognised including instalments on naval construction contracts under the percentage-of-completion method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include PE-generated income from containers vessel construction; attach PE accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Personnel expenses: wages, salaries, social security costs for naval architects, engineers, welders, and production staff.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses economically linked to the PE; allocate headcount costs appropriately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net financial expense: borrowings used for working capital and ship construction financing, subject to Article 16 LIS deductibility limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE interest deductions follow thin-capitalisation rules; include only interest linked to PE activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before prior-year loss offset: accounting profit adjusted for permanent and temporary differences under the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE's taxable base is computed using Spanish GAAP and LIS rules; transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits applied: R&D tax credits, shipbuilding investment credits, and double-taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits connected to PE income and Spanish activities are claimable; non-residents without PE cannot claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 5% of the tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 9 months, and 20% after 12 months; plus late-payment interest accruing daily. Fixed penalty of €200 for filing without tax due; administrative penalties of 50% of the evaded amount if fraudulent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 202 (Modelo 202) – Corporate income tax instalment payment return; submitted electronically through AEAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly / Early payment (three instalments per year for calendar-year taxpayers; some taxpayers use monthly instalments)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers: 20 April, 20 October, and 20 December. For non-calendar fiscal years, the deadlines mirror the corresponding months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base for the instalment period: profit attributable to the year-to-date period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments based on the PE's prior-year taxable base or profit share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable instalment rate: generally 18% for entities with net turnover of at least €10 million, or 17% for the first year; certain entities use 25% on the prior-year tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE uses the same calculation rules as resident taxpayers when filing Form 202.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable: resulting instalment after credits and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE must remit tax attributable to Spanish-source income; no foreign tax offset in instalment stage.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late instalment surcharge of 5% to 20% plus daily late-payment interest; denial of instalment deductions in annual return if omitted; penalties for incorrect instalment calculation up to 50% of the unpaid instalment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For distributions to non-resident shareholders: 19% for beneficiaries resident in an EU/EEA state with reciprocity, and 24% for beneficiaries resident outside the EU/EEA, unless a tax treaty provides a lower rate. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies when the parent holds at least 5% of the Spanish company for 12 months, resulting in 0% withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficiary must obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction and submit it to the withholding agent before payment. The agent applies the treaty rate on Form 216 (refund procedure) or Form 211 (annual summary). Where excess withholding has occurred, the beneficiary may file a refund claim with the AEAT within the four-year limitation period using Form 100 (IRNR return).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties: 19% for EU/EEA residents and 24% for third-country residents, reduced under applicable treaties (commonly 10% or 0% for industrial royalties). Statutory withholding on interest: 19% for EU/EEA residents and 24% for third-country residents, treaty rates often 10% or 5% for bank interest; interest to non-resident financial institutions under syndicated shipbuilding loans may be exempt under EU Interest and Royalties Directive conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR: Local File and Master File are mandatory for taxpayers whose net turnover in the preceding 12 months equals or exceeds €10 million. A Country-by-Country Report is required for the ultimate parent of a multinational group with consolidated revenue of at least €750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not implement the offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations but enforces economic substance requirements through the General Anti-Abuse Rule (DTA), Controlled Foreign Company rules (Art. 100 LIS), and the European anti-tax avoidance directive (ATAD). A Spanish SL operating as an ocean container vessel shipyard must demonstrate physical premises, qualified workforce, budget, and actual risk management. Artificial structures lacking these facts will be disregarded for tax purposes and the income reattributed to the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraud against the Spanish Tax Agency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting invoiced shipbuilding revenue, falsifying construction costs, or manipulating transfer prices with related shipyards to understate taxable base by more than €120,000 in a single tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law (Organic Law 10/1995, art. 305): imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the defrauded amount; aggravated penalty of 4 to 7 years if the fraud uses offshore vehicles or exceeds €600,000. Administrative penalty of 50% of the omitted tax plus late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax declarations or use interposed companies are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, face monetary fines, seizure of personal assets, travel bans, disqualification from public benefits and subsidies, and imprisonment up to 6 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Spanish SL with no functioning shipyard, no marine engineering staff, and no operational activity; using it solely to route container-vessel sale proceeds and access favourable tax provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the General Anti-Abuse Rule: the arrangement is nullified, income is re-apportioned to the real profit earner, and a penalty of 50% of the undercharged tax is imposed. If the resulting revenue shortfall exceeds the criminal threshold, prosecution under art. 305 ensues.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Administrators of the artificial entity incur personal liability for the underlying tax liabilities, including disqualification from holding board positions up to 10 years, monetary fines, and possible extradition via criminal investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using shipyard contracts and maritime escrow accounts to layer illicit funds, issue fictitious commissions to foreign suppliers, or conceal settlement payments in off-shore non-cooperative jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 10/2010: administrative fines up to €1,000,000 or two to five times the laundered amount. Criminal Code art. 301: imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years, fines of 3 times the value of the assets, and possible dissolution of the legal entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors engaged in laundering face criminal conviction, attachment of personal estates, travel bans under court order, and lifting of the corporate veil to allow civil suits by affected creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / Non-submission of Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting the annual Form 200 or quarterly instalment payment despite generating taxable Spanish-source profit from shipyard operations, or filing after the statutory deadline without a valid excuse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing surcharge of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6 months), 15% (within 9 months), and 20% (after 12 months) of the tax due; fixed penalty of €200 for returns showing zero balance; daily late-payment interest; administrative penalty of 50% of the omitted amount if authorities detect the omission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with management responsibility are jointly liable for the late-payment surcharge and interest; if the hidden tax exceeds €120,000, criminal liability may be imposed, including prison sentences of 2 to 6 years and prohibition from receiving subsidies.
